target.title: fix(msteams): strip internal tool-trace banners from outbound text
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Microsoft Teams outbound adapter did not strip internal tool-trace banners
from assistant-visible text before delivery. Users could see internal
scaffolding like `⚠️ 🛠️ search repos (agent) failed` in Teams messages.

## Why This Change Was Made

Added `sanitizeAssistantVisibleText` (the canonical shared sanitizer) to
`msteamsChannelOutbound` via the `sanitizeText` hook. This matches the fix
already applied to tlon (#103450) and synology-chat (#102925).

The `msteamsOutbound` in `outbound.ts` is a runtime delegate (exposes
sendText/sendMedia/sendPayload) — it does not need `sanitizeText` because
the delivery pipeline invokes the hook on `msteamsChannelOutbound`.

## User Impact

**Before:** internal tool-trace banners visible in Teams messages
**After:** internal scaffolding stripped, only user-visible prose delivered

## Evidence

Branch: `fix/msteams-sanitize-outbound` | Base: `upstream/main`

### Real behavior proof

The plugin-level tests assert against `msteamsPlugin.outbound.sanitizeText`
which routes to `msteamsChannelOutbound` — the exact production adapter the
delivery pipeline invokes. The test verifies:
- Tool-trace banners are stripped ("Done.\n⚠️ 🛠️ `search repos (agent)` failed" → "Done.")
- Normal prose passes through unchanged
- Trace-only replies become empty strings

### Regression tests

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/msteams/src/channel.test.ts --reporter=verbose

 ✓ msteamsPlugin > advertises sanitizeText that strips internal tool-trace banners from outbound text
 ✓ msteamsPlugin > sanitizeText returns empty string for trace-only replies

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  18 passed (18)
```

### Diff summary

```
extensions/msteams/src/channel.ts       | 4 ++ (import + sanitizeText hook)
extensions/msteams/src/channel.test.ts  | 12 ++ (2 regression tests)
```

What was not tested: live Microsoft Teams transport (requires a registered
Teams bot with Azure Bot Framework). The test exercises the exact production
callback that the delivery pipeline invokes — the same proof pattern accepted
for tlon (#103450) and synology-chat (#102925).

- [x] I understand what the code does
- [x] Change is focused and does not mix unrelated concerns
